teaching.hint: Can a whole-bitset flip be represented without touching every stored bit immediately?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A global complement flag reinterprets stored bits in constant time, while a logical one-count answers aggregate queries.
solution_outline.approach: Store physical bits, a complement flag, and the current logical one-count. Translate individual writes through the flag, toggle the flag and complement the count on `flip`, and materialize a string only on `toString`.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The logical value at each index is its stored bit XOR the flag, and the count equals the number of logical ones after every operation.
solution_outline.correctness: Construction establishes the invariant. Individual updates preserve it at one index, a flip complements all logical values and changes the count to `size−count`, and every query reads the resulting logical state.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(1)` time for all operations except `toString`, which takes `O(size)`; `O(size)` storage. At most five materializations occur.
solution_outline.pitfall: After a flip, changing a stored bit without translating through the flag can reverse the requested logical update.

common_wrong_turns: Physically scan every bit on each flip
Change the one-count for an idempotent fix/unfix
source_fidelity_notes: The five-call cap on `toString` and index-to-character order are retained.
